target_customer: Engineering and product teams that run AI agents (Cursor, AgentKit) over internal company data
problem: Agents need secure, permissioned access to internal tools like Slack, Confluence, Drive, HubSpot and Jira, and wiring that up per agent is slow and risky.
business_model: Developer and enterprise SaaS, free to start, paid tiers not documented
product_category: Data gateway and access control for AI agents

founders.name: Kevin Treehan
founders.background_notes: YC page: he and Rohan have known each other five years from Exeter and Yale.

founders.name: Rohan Radhakeesoon
founders.background_notes: YC profile and his bio disagree on the title.

technical_complexity.rationale: Connectors, per-tool filtering, role based access and monitoring across many SaaS APIs is standard integration engineering with security-sensitive parts.

defensibility.rationale: Connector breadth and permission models create some lock-in, but open protocols like MCP and funded platforms make the wedge easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Search results show multiple funded MCP gateway and agent tooling companies in 2025 and 2026 (Obot 35M seed Sept 2025, Arcade 60M Series A 2026). No action against Capacitive found.

market_need_then: Rapid growth of coding and workflow agents in 2025 created demand for governed access to internal data; no Capacitive-specific demand evidence found.

identity.visual_style: minimal site with only name and contact

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found and the company site shows almost no content.

outcome_analysis: Capacitive is an active two person Spring 2025 company whose public beta was scheduled for May 30, 2025. No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found and no funding is verified. The category of agent data gateways filled with funded competitors during 2025 and 2026, so its prospects are unclear from public data.
notes: Funding conflicts: VCBacked and ChoppingBlock list 500K (matches standard YC deal), StartupIntros mentions Scott Belsky as an angel, StartupHub says 12M total; none confirmed by a company or press source, so no round recorded. No competitor source dated near the batch was found (the found coverage is from late 2025 and 2026), so the list is empty. The company site shows only name and contact.
